chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man shortens the prayer during a journey of twelve miles.'
And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in what distance is the prayer shortened? He said: 'In a Breeed. Do you not see that the people of Mecca, when they go out to 'Arafah, are required to shorten the prayer?'
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man, from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about shortening the prayer, so he said: 'In four Farasikh.'
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Mu'awiya ibn Hukaym, from Abu Malik al-Hadrami, from Abu al-Jarud, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in what distance is the shortening? He said: 'In a Breeed.'

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: Shortening of the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs during travel
key_terms.بَرِيدٌ: A traditional unit of distance, approximately 4-5 miles
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: Arafah, the site of the Hajj ritual, used here as a benchmark for travel distance
key_terms.فَرَاسِخَ: Plural of Farasikh, a unit of distance equal to four Farasikh (approx. 12-15 miles)
key_terms.مِيلًا: Miles (plural of Mil, a unit of distance)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum distance for shortening prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: These narrations from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarify the specific travel distance (masafat al-tahrir) required to shorten the four-rak'ah prayers, with the Imams offering consistent measurements such as four Farasikh or a Breeed. The reference to the journey to 'Arafah underscores the practical application of this rule in major pilgrimage contexts, reflecting the Shia scholarly consensus on the quantifiable threshold for Qasr.
